root_cause_label: Visual Perception Incapability Leading to Arbitrary Move Submission
one_sentence_failure_summary: Unable to parse the chess board from the PNG image using ASCII rendering (which produced only uninterpretable pixel noise), the agent abandoned all further recovery strategies and wrote an arbitrary standard opening move 'e2e4' to /app/move.txt without any grounding in the actual position.
t_err_evidence: At step 9, the agent explicitly acknowledged failure ('terminal rendering produced too much output to reliably parse the position') and chose to output 'e2e4' as a 'standard strong opening move for White' despite having no knowledge of the actual board position — a decision based on no factual grounding.
t_commit_evidence: The command 'printf "e2e4\n" > /app/move.txt' at step 9 writes the wrong answer to the output file and locks in failure; from this point, the agent only signals completion and cannot recover.
t_surface_evidence: Writing 'e2e4' to /app/move.txt at step 9 is the first observable manifestation of wrong output — the arbitrary move will not match the actual best move(s) for the specific board position.
trigger_explanation: The agent had a reasonable multi-step plan (check metadata, use strings, render as ASCII via Pillow and chafa) but the actual image rendering tools available in the terminal environment produced only visual noise from which no piece positions could be reliably identified. This is a model-level visual perception limit: the approach of converting a chess board PNG to terminal ASCII is fundamentally insufficient for reliable piece identification at any ASCII resolution, and the agent lacked the domain knowledge to pivot to a more effective approach (e.g., chess-specific image recognition libraries or installing Stockfish with a board-parsing pipeline).
forewarning_evidence: At step 7, the ASCII rendering produced a garbled pattern of '#', '+', '=', and other symbols that does not resemble a readable chess board. At step 8, the enhanced binary and multi-ramp views produced similarly uninterpretable output. Both outputs clearly signal that the approach cannot recover the board state, yet the agent continued without pivoting to an alternative strategy.
